clue.text: They may have nights out on the tiles

definitions.text: They may have nights out on the tiles

parts.words: They may have nights out on the tiles
parts.note: a night on the tiles is a wild night out, and male cats literally prowl the roof tiles at night

explanation.surface: A remark about revellers who stay out partying all night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the tiles' is a British idiom for a night of carousing; taken literally it puts you on a rooftop, where tomcats roam.
explanation.definitionFit: Male cats famously roam rooftops yowling at night, which is where the partying idiom comes from.

clue.text: Deceive company? On occasion

parts.note: from the saying 'two's company', company means a pair
an occasion is a time, as in 'that one time'

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a firm sometimes cheats people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' looks like a business, but it is the 'two's company' saying; 'On' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be unfaithful to a partner, cheating on them with someone else, is to deceive them.

clue.text: Set off on horseback?

definitions.meaning: a jewel or picture is displayed to advantage when placed in a setting or frame
riders sitting in the saddle are said to be up on their horses

explanation.surface: A question whether someone departed riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set off' reads as departing, but it means displayed in a frame or setting.
explanation.definitionFit: A gem fixed in a ring is held in a setting, and a rider in the saddle is likewise up and seated.

clue.text: Jumping bail, I must make an excuse

indicators.note: jumping suggests letters leaping about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A defendant who skipped bail needs a good story to explain it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumping bail' is a real legal phrase, which disguises 'Jumping' as the anagram signal on BAIL and I.
explanation.definitionFit: An account showing you were elsewhere at the time is the classic excuse offered to clear yourself.

clue.text: Could be put into a suit case

indicators.note: could be put suggests the letters may be placed in a different order

explanation.surface: A remark about packing a suit into a piece of luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit case' looks like luggage, but 'case' alone is the definition, and INTO A SUIT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: In phrases like 'in that case', the word means the state of affairs or circumstances.

clue.text: It has a back-breaking job keeping down vermin

definitions.text: It has a back-breaking job keeping down vermin

parts.words: It has a back-breaking job keeping down vermin
parts.note: a spring device for pests snaps down and literally breaks the rodent's back, controlling the vermin population

explanation.surface: A sympathetic description of a pest controller's gruelling work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-breaking' sounds like hard labour, but the sprung bar of the device really does break a rodent's back.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring-loaded device is set to catch rodents, keeping their numbers in check.

clue.text: Knave withdrawn from the pack?

definitions.meaning: a knave is a dishonest scoundrel or rascal
an elephant or wolf living apart from its herd or pack is described this way

explanation.surface: A question whether the jack has been taken out of a deck of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knave' and 'pack' suggest playing cards, but the senses are a scoundrel and a solitary animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a scoundrel, and a lone animal driven out of its herd is a solitary outcast.

clue.text: Ruth uses a new reference book

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: Ruth consults a newly bought reference volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of synonyms is a standard reference work for writers.

clue.text: Understand that lies are wrong

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters are in a mistaken order and need putting right

explanation.surface: Grasp the moral point that telling untruths is bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a link word; LIES and ARE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to grasp or comprehend something is a synonym of understanding it.

clue.text: Kind of concrete that takes woven carpets

indicators.note: woven suggests strands of the word being worked into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A sort of building material used under woven rugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that takes' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Concrete cast into blocks or panels in a factory before installation is described this way.

clue.text: His visitors may take a dim view of him at first

definitions.text: His visitors may take a dim view of him at first

parts.words: His visitors may take a dim view of him at first
parts.note: patients of an eye specialist arrive with poor sight, so they literally see him dimly before treatment

explanation.surface: A professional whose clients initially disapprove of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take a dim view' normally means disapprove; here it is literal, poor eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor is visited by people whose vision is blurred.

clue.text: It should have a safety pin in it

definitions.text: It should have a safety pin in it

parts.words: It should have a safety pin in it
parts.note: a hand-thrown bomb has a pin that stops it going off until pulled

explanation.surface: Advice about fastening something, like a nappy, with a safety pin.
explanation.walkthrough: A safety pin suggests clothing, but here it is the pin that keeps a bomb from exploding.
explanation.definitionFit: This hand-thrown explosive is armed by pulling out its pin.

clue.text: Entangled but certain it can be unravelled

indicators.note: unravelled suggests a knot of letters being untangled into another order

explanation.surface: A knotty problem that is sure to be solved.
explanation.definitionFit: Something complicated and full of interwoven detail is tangled up.

clue.text: A girl returns with a new name

indicators.note: returns means the phrase is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: A girl comes back with a fresh name.
explanation.walkthrough: A TINA read backwards gives a different girl's name, so 'a new name' is the definition and 'with' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's first name, formed fresh from the reversal.

clue.text: Finally attain a high position

definitions.meaning: upright, with the top end raised

explanation.surface: Reach the top job at last.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means to arrive eventually, and also standing on end, raised up.

clue.text: Source of income for a school head

definitions.meaning: the capital sum invested, which earns interest
the head teacher of a school or college

explanation.surface: A headteacher's salary as a source of earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Invested capital yields interest, and a college head holds this title.

clue.text: Tense seconds are, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense of past continuous action
seconds are factory goods with flaws, sold cheap

explanation.surface: A nervous remark about time ticking by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' and 'seconds' suggest anxiety and time; they are grammar and flawed goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical tense has this name, and flawed goods are faulty.

clue.text: What workers do in their bloomers

definitions.text: What workers do in their bloomers

parts.words: What workers do in their bloomers
parts.note: worker bees carry pollen between flowers, the plants that bloom

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about labourers in old-fashioned knickers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomers' are baggy underwear, but here flowers; 'workers' are worker bees.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees fertilise flowers by transferring pollen.

clue.text: Coastline spoilt in parts

indicators.note: spoilt suggests the word is damaged and its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Ruined stretches of the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Made of separate pieces fitted together, like a modular sofa.

clue.text: Representative-a good man, and popular

parts.note: a saint is a good man, abbreviated ST

explanation.surface: A delegate described as a decent, well-liked fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute acting in someone's place represents them.

clue.text: House with a bed and a broken gate

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: broken suggests the word is smashed and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: A home with a bed inside and a damaged gate outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rural dwelling is a kind of house.

clue.text: The setting for confrontation

definitions.meaning: the place where a story or play's action happens
a noisy public row, as in 'make a fuss'

explanation.surface: The location for a showdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A play's location is its backdrop, and a public row is an embarrassing display.

clue.text: It alone can provide a sense of euphoria

indicators.note: can provide suggests the letters may be rearranged to supply something new

explanation.surface: Only this thing brings blissful happiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Great joy and high spirits are the same feeling as euphoria.

clue.text: Level betting includes the French teams

indicators.note: includes means one piece takes another inside it

parts.note: evens is betting odds of one to one

explanation.surface: Even odds offered on French sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket and football sides have eleven players each.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football sides of that many players are known by this word.

clue.text: It can turn into quite a lark

indicators.note: turn into suggests the letters change into something else by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Something that might become great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A playful caper or prank is a bit of fun.

clue.text: Start to make a speech without a single drink

indicators.note: without here means outside, one piece placed around the others

parts.note: to orate is to deliver a speech
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Begin addressing the crowd without having had a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here is the old sense of outside, not lacking, so the speech wraps around the single drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin or arise from a source is to start.

clue.text: Had conceded

explanation.definitionFit: It means possessed, and also admitted, as in owning up to a fault.

clue.text: Send down under

parts.note: not a trip to Australia but placing a body in the earth

explanation.surface: Deport someone to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' suggests Australia; it means beneath the ground, burial.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to place it beneath the ground.

clue.text: Poker-faced, departed to search for gold

parts.note: prospectors pan river gravel for gold

explanation.surface: An expressionless prospector, now deceased.
explanation.definitionFit: Expressionless, without showing emotion, as a card player keeps a blank face.

clue.text: Straddling a step?

parts.note: a stride is a long step

explanation.surface: Taking a big step with legs apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with a leg on each side, as on a horse.

clue.text: Irritated when necessity took first place

explanation.surface: Annoyed when urgency took priority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Pricked or provoked into annoyance.

clue.text: Jobs for the boys

parts.note: not favouritism, but tasks given to delivery lads who run messages

explanation.surface: Cronyism, giving posts to friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jobs for the boys' is a British idiom for nepotism; here it is literal tasks for messenger boys.
explanation.definitionFit: Short trips to deliver messages or buy things were run by message boys.
